title: Health snapshot and customer playbook for eu-west-1 streaming disruption
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a concise customer-facing playbook and status snapshot for the streaming degradation that affected requests served from eu-west-1 on 2029-05-01. Use this as the canonical copy for: (1) a short status page update, (2) an email to directly impacted accounts, and (3) a one-page post-incident summary for account teams.

Executive summary (one line):
On 2029-05-01 at ~09:23 UTC Redwood observed degraded streaming responses from eu-west-1 for long-running streaming sessions; we rolled back a runtime scheduler change and deployed a hotfix, returning streaming to normal by 2029-05-01 13:10 UTC.

What happened (customer language):
- Impact: Some streaming sessions (responses > ~2k tokens, high concurrency) experienced partial truncation, delayed first tokens, or abrupt session termination. Non-streaming completions and embeddings were mostly unaffected.
- Who: A subset of hosted-API customers and any self-serve accounts routing to eu-west-1 were affected intermittently between ~09:20–13:10 UTC.
- Data integrity: There is no indication of data loss or leakage. No user content was exposed.

Immediate actions we took (timeline):
- 2029-05-01 09:20 UTC: Monitoring alerted on elevated stream disconnects and higher 5xx rates for streaming endpoints in eu-west-1.
- 2029-05-01 09:32 UTC: Incident declared, on-call and runtime leads paged.
- 2029-05-01 09:50 UTC: Short-term mitigation: throttled new long-lived streaming sessions on affected pools to reduce scheduler pressure.
- 2029-05-01 10:40 UTC: Identified regression in continuous-batching scheduler that caused missed heartbeat/keepalive for streaming shards under high concurrency (regression introduced by INF-4821).
- 2029-05-01 11:15 UTC: Emergency rollback of scheduler change to the prior stable config across eu-west-1; service error rates reduced.
- 2029-05-01 12:05 UTC: Deployed hotfix to heartbeat handling and added guardrails to session lifecycle logic (PR #768).
- 2029-05-01 13:10 UTC: Observed stabilized streaming metrics; monitoring returned to baseline.

Short status page copy (concise):
Headline: "Streaming degraded in eu-west-1 — partial resolution in progress"
Impact: "Between 09:20–13:10 UTC some streaming sessions routed to eu-west-1 experienced truncated or interrupted responses. Non-streaming requests were largely unaffected."
Current status: "Resolved — rolling fixes applied and monitoring normal. Final post-incident summary will be posted in 3 business days."
What we did: "Rolled back a scheduling change and deployed a heartbeat fix to prevent session drops; increased observability on streaming heartbeats."
Recommended customer actions: "If you rely on long-lived streaming sessions in eu-west-1, validate any resumed sessions for unexpected truncation and re-run critical prompts. If you need assistance, contact your account team or support@redwood.ai with 'eu-west-1 streaming' in the subject."

Email copy for impacted accounts (short):
Subject: "Update: eu-west-1 streaming disruption (May 1) — service restored"
Body:
Hi <Account Team>,

We wanted to let you know we resolved an issue that intermittently impacted streaming responses for requests routed to eu-west-1 on May 1. We rolled back a scheduler change and deployed a patch that prevents session keepalive drops. The incident window was ~09:20–13:10 UTC and we have confirmed metrics are normal.

Action items for you: re-run any interrupted critical flows and reach out if you see residual truncation.

If you'd like help validating traffic or want a scoped replay of impacted requests, reply to this message and we will prioritize.

Sincerely,
Maya Chen
Customer Success

One-page post-incident summary for customers (structure):
- Impact summary: timeframe, affected endpoints, % of requests impacted (approx).
- Root cause (non-technical and technical): short explanation of the scheduler regression and heartbeat drop.
- Scope: list of affected models/endpoints (we will enumerate per-account in follow-ups).
- Mitigations performed: rollback, hotfix, increased monitoring, autoscaling guardrails adjustment.
- Remediation plan: permanent changes, additional validation gates in CI, and model of future scheduler rollout (staged canary + synthetic streaming load tests).
- Compensation/credits: standard credit offer for degraded SLA windows; account teams will propose credit in line with contract.
- Contacts and next steps: named owners and an expected date for the detailed technical writeup (target: 2029-05-06).

Sample technical root cause paragraph (customer-friendly):
A change to the scheduler that optimizes batching under low-latency conditions caused an unintended interaction with streaming session heartbeat logic. Under high concurrency that interaction occasionally prevented timely heartbeat renewal, so streaming sessions were prematurely closed. The change passed unit and functional tests but did not get sufficient end-to-end stress coverage for long-lived streaming patterns.

Q&A for account teams (anticipated customer questions):
Q: Were any user messages lost?
A: There is no evidence of data loss. Interrupted streams may have been truncated; we can re-run or reprocess if you need assistance.

Q: Will this happen again?
A: We have rolled back the risky change, released a fix that defends heartbeats, and added synthetic long-lived stream tests to our regression suite. We will also gate similar scheduler changes behind staged rollouts and longer canaries.

Q: What about other regions?
A: We audited other regions and did not observe the same failure mode; the change was deployed globally but the failure was only reproducible under eu-west-1 traffic patterns.

Internal playbook notes (ops-oriented):
- Owner for customer comms: Maya Chen (CS).
- Technical owner for remediation updates: Evan Zhu (runtime).
- Billing / credits owner: Sofia Martinez (CS/Billing).
- Next internal checkpoint: 2029-05-04 10:00 UTC sync between runtime, SRE, and CS for final post-incident review.
- Attachments to finalize before customer send: per-account impact table (CSV), exact list of affected endpoint IDs, sample logs for one https session.

Draft action items (who/what/when):
- Evan: complete postmortem writeup and root-cause diagram by 2029-05-05.
- Runtime: add long-lived stream synthetic tests to CI and a canary that simulates 1k concurrent streams by 2029-05-20.
- CS: prepare tailored outreach for top 10 impacted accounts by 2029-05-04.

Notes / links:
- Jira: INF-4821 (scheduler change that was rolled back)
- GitHub PR: serving-runtime PR #768 (heartbeat fix)
- Slack incident channel: #inc-eu-west1 (live notes and timeline)

Tone guidance:
- Be explicit about impact and what customers must do (replay important prompts).
- Avoid overly technical jargon in customer-facing text; use the technical paragraph only for customers that request it.
- Commit to a specific date for a detailed technical postmortem (target included above).

Draft status: internal draft — ready for engineering accuracy pass and legal review before sending to customers.
